title: Wiring a Reachy Mini into OpenClaw without trusting the robot
why_read: A hands-on account of wiring a home robot to a personal AI assistant with a thoughtful security-conscious architecture decision, useful as a real-world agent security case study.
analysis: The author describes integrating a Reachy Mini desktop robot, running on a Raspberry Pi with an HTTP API, into their existing home automation and LLM assistant setup called OpenClaw. Notably, they explicitly reconsidered a naive 'agent controls robot directly' architecture for trust and security reasons, which is a genuinely useful design consideration as more people connect LLM agents to physical actuators in the home. The piece is anecdotal and specific to one hobbyist setup rather than a generalized framework, but the security reasoning around not blindly trusting robot control loops is a valuable, underdiscussed topic.
